examples.meeting_summary:
Meeting: Discovery call — Inventory & Purchasing Platform for Norte Distribuciones
Date: 2026-03-10 | Duration: 75 min
Attendees (client): COO, Head of Warehouse Operations, Purchasing Manager, IT Coordinator (one person, part-time)
Attendees (us): Account Manager, Tech Lead, Product Designer

## 1. Context and problem
Norte Distribuciones is a mid-size distributor of industrial spare parts (about 12,000 active SKUs, 3 warehouses in two cities, 45 employees, about 600 orders/day). Inventory is tracked today in shared Excel files plus a 12-year-old desktop ERP (SAP Business One 9.3, on-premise) that is only used for invoicing. Consequences reported by the client: frequent stock-outs of fast-moving parts, about 4% mismatch between physical and recorded stock, purchase orders created by email, and no visibility of stock across warehouses. Stock counts take 2 full days per quarter.

## 2. Goal
Replace the spreadsheets with a web-based inventory and purchasing platform that gives real-time stock per warehouse, tracks every stock movement, automates reorder suggestions, and manages purchase orders end to end. Success criteria stated by the client: stock accuracy above 98%, stock-outs of top-200 SKUs reduced by 50% within 6 months, quarterly count reduced to 1 day.

## 3. In scope (MVP)
- Product catalog: SKUs with variants, categories, units of measure, supplier(s), min/max stock levels. Bulk CSV import/export.
- Multi-warehouse and bin-location management (3 warehouses, about 40 locations each).
- Stock movements ledger: goods receipt, issue, transfer between warehouses, manual adjustment with reason. Every movement is immutable and audited.
- Purchase orders: supplier management, PO creation, approval flow (2 levels above a configurable amount), partial receipts, PDF/email to supplier.
- Low-stock alerts and reorder suggestions based on min levels and last-90-day consumption.
- Barcode support: generate labels (Code128) and scan with the phone camera from the browser (no native app).
- Dashboard: stock value, stock-outs, slow movers, open POs, movements per day. Reports exportable to CSV/XLSX.
- Roles: Admin, Warehouse Operator, Purchasing, Read-only (manager). Login with the client's Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC SSO).
- One-way sync of products and stock levels to the existing SAP B1, running hourly (confirmed in the call).
- One-time migration of current Excel data.
- UI in Spanish and English.

## 4. Out of scope (explicit)
Sales orders / e-commerce, invoicing, native mobile apps, offline mode, demand forecasting with ML, RFID, multi-currency accounting, supplier portal, lot/serial/expiry tracking (confirmed not needed), hardware procurement (scanners, label printers; the client buys them).

## 5. Constraints
- Budget ceiling communicated informally: about USD 55k.
- Hard deadline: go-live before the high season starting 2026-09-01, so development must finish by mid-July at the latest. Kickoff is planned for 2026-04-06.
- Data residency: data must stay in the AWS sa-east-1 (Sao Paulo) region.
- The IT Coordinator is only available about 4 h/week; business stakeholders can attend one weekly 1-hour demo/feedback session.
- Warehouse Wi-Fi is unreliable in one location; the UI must tolerate slow connections (no offline mode, but retries and clear error states).
- Users are not technical: the main flows (receive, issue, transfer) must take at most 3 taps/clicks from the home screen on a phone.
- Target scale: up to 15 concurrent users, 12k SKUs, about 2,000 movements/day, 5 years of history.

## 6. Proposed stack
- Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, Tailwind + component library, PWA for camera scanning (ZXing).
- Backend: Node.js 20 + NestJS (REST, OpenAPI), PostgreSQL 15 (RDS), Prisma ORM, BullMQ + Redis for background jobs (imports, alerts, ERP sync).
- Auth: Microsoft Entra ID via OIDC, roles mapped from groups.
- Infra: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SES, CloudWatch), Terraform, GitHub Actions CI/CD, 3 environments (dev, staging, prod).
- Quality: Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright, Sentry.

## 7. Integrations
- Microsoft Entra ID (SSO): client IT already has a tenant and will create the app registration.
- SAP Business One 9.3 on-premise: the Service Layer is enabled (confirmed by client IT during the call). Access from AWS goes through a site-to-site VPN that client IT will provide; sync is one-way (platform to SAP) and hourly.
- Amazon SES for email; supplier email templates provided by the client.

## 8. Assumptions
- Client provides Excel data within 2 weeks of kickoff; data cleaning of up to 12k rows is done by the client, we only validate and load it.
- A single approval workflow (configurable threshold), not a generic workflow engine.
- Up to 18 distinct screens in the high-fidelity design; the client has no brand guide beyond a logo.
- Client feedback within 2 business days; one consolidated round of changes per demo.
- 2 UAT cycles of 1 week each, executed by the client.
- Purchase order approval: orders up to USD 2,000 are approved by the Purchasing Manager; above that, the COO also approves. The threshold is configurable by an Admin.
- Reports beyond the dashboard: 5 reports (stock by warehouse, movements by period, slow movers, supplier performance, open POs).
- The client provides the label printer (Zebra, 100x50 mm labels) and the scanners; Bluetooth/USB HID scanners work as keyboard input with no extra development.
- Spanish/English scope includes the UI, emails and PDFs.
- Support after hypercare is out of this estimate and handled under a separate agreement.

## 9. Risks
- HIGH: SAP B1 9.3 is an old version; the Service Layer is enabled but the integration depends on the client's VPN and on SAP-side permissions being granted on time.
- HIGH: Data quality of the Excel files (duplicate SKUs, inconsistent units) may delay migration and the stock accuracy goal.
- MEDIUM: Limited client availability (IT 4 h/week) can block SSO setup, VPN and UAT.
- MEDIUM: Budget (about 55k) is tight relative to scope; scope creep around reports and approval rules is likely.
- MEDIUM: Browser camera barcode scanning is less reliable on low-end Android devices and in low light; the fallback is a USB/Bluetooth HID scanner.
- LOW: Fixed go-live date before high season leaves little slack; any delay in kickoff impacts directly.
examples.estimation:
## Estimate: Inventory & Purchasing Platform for Norte Distribuciones

### Task breakdown:

**Phase 0 — Discovery, setup and infrastructure** (90 hours)
1. Kickoff, requirements refinement and backlog grooming: 16 hours
2. Technical architecture and ADRs (auth, multi-warehouse model, ledger design): 12 hours
3. Monorepo setup, linting, CI pipeline (GitHub Actions: build, test, lint): 14 hours
4. AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform (VPC, ECS, RDS, Redis, S3, SES) for dev/staging/prod: 28 hours
5. CD pipelines, environment config and secrets management: 10 hours
6. Observability: structured logging, Sentry, CloudWatch dashboards and alarms: 10 hours

**Phase 1 — UX/UI design** (94 hours)
7. User flows and low-fi wireframes for main journeys (receive, issue, transfer, PO, count): 20 hours
8. Design system: tokens, base components, mobile-first patterns: 16 hours
9. High-fidelity design of ~18 screens (desktop + mobile): 36 hours
10. Clickable prototype and usability review with warehouse operators: 12 hours
11. Design iterations after feedback and developer handoff: 10 hours

**Phase 2 — Backend** (362 hours)
12. Database schema design, migrations and seed data: 16 hours
13. Authentication: Entra ID OIDC, session/JWT handling, group-to-role mapping: 20 hours
14. RBAC for 4 roles with permission guards on all endpoints: 12 hours
15. Product catalog API: SKUs, variants, categories, units of measure, suppliers: 28 hours
16. Warehouse and bin-location management API: 14 hours
17. Stock movements ledger: receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments with transactional integrity and concurrency control: 44 hours
18. Stock level queries and per-warehouse/per-location availability (materialized views / indexes): 16 hours
19. Supplier management API: 10 hours
20. Purchase orders API: lifecycle, 2-level approval, partial receipts: 36 hours
21. PO PDF generation and email to supplier via SES (ES/EN templates): 14 hours
22. Reorder suggestion engine and low-stock alerts (scheduled BullMQ jobs): 20 hours
23. Barcode label generation (Code128, PDF label sheets) and lookup endpoint: 12 hours
24. Immutable audit log for all state-changing operations: 12 hours
25. CSV bulk import/export with validation, error report and async processing: 24 hours
26. Dashboard and reports API (5 reports + KPIs), CSV/XLSX export: 28 hours
27. SAP Business One one-way sync (Service Layer client over VPN, hourly job, mapping, retries, reconciliation): 48 hours
28. API documentation (OpenAPI), pagination, filtering and error conventions: 8 hours

**Phase 3 — Frontend** (250 hours)
29. App shell, routing, API client generation from OpenAPI, state/query setup: 16 hours
30. Login flow, role-based route guards and session expiry handling: 12 hours
31. Catalog screens: list with filters/search, detail, create/edit, variants: 28 hours
32. Warehouses and locations screens: 12 hours
33. Stock overview and movement screens (receive, issue, transfer, adjust) optimized for mobile: 34 hours
34. Purchase order screens: list, create, approval, receive goods, supplier management: 34 hours
35. Dashboard with KPI tiles and charts: 24 hours
36. Reports screens with filters and export: 14 hours
37. Camera barcode scanning in the browser (PWA, ZXing) with HID scanner support: 20 hours
38. Import wizard: upload, column mapping, validation preview, error download: 18 hours
39. Alerts / notification center and reorder suggestions view: 12 hours
40. Internationalization (ES/EN) for all screens: 10 hours
41. Responsive polish, accessibility pass (WCAG AA basics), slow-connection states: 16 hours

**Phase 4 — Quality assurance** (194 hours)
42. Backend unit tests (ledger, PO workflow, reorder engine at high coverage): 30 hours
43. Backend integration tests against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers): 24 hours
44. Frontend component and hook tests: 18 hours
45. E2E tests with Playwright for critical flows (login, receive, transfer, PO approval, import): 24 hours
46. Performance and load testing (15 concurrent users, 12k SKUs, 2k movements/day) and query tuning: 14 hours
47. Security review: OWASP checklist, dependency scanning, secrets and IAM review: 12 hours
48. Manual QA and regression (2 cycles) on desktop and low-end Android devices: 32 hours
49. UAT support and bug fixing (2 cycles of 1 week): 40 hours

**Phase 5 — Migration, deployment and handover** (88 hours)
50. Excel data analysis, mapping, migration scripts and dry runs: 28 hours
51. Production deployment, cutover runbook and rollback plan: 12 hours
52. Documentation: user guide (ES), admin guide, technical runbook: 16 hours
53. Training: 2 sessions (warehouse and purchasing/admin), recorded: 8 hours
54. Hypercare (2 weeks): bug fixing and on-call support: 24 hours

**Phase 6 — Project management** (90 hours)
55. Project management, weekly demos, status reports, client coordination (~11%): 90 hours

**Subtotal: 1168 hours**
**Contingency (15%, driven by SAP B1 and data-quality risks): 180 hours**
**Total estimate: 1348 hours**

### Recommended team:
- 1 Tech Lead / senior full-stack (full-time, about 10 weeks equivalent)
- 2 full-stack developers (full-time)
- 1 Product Designer (part-time, Phases 1 and 3 support)
- 1 QA engineer (part-time from week 7)
- 1 Project Manager (part-time)

### Estimated duration: 14–16 weeks (3.5–4 months) from kickoff, including 2 weeks of hypercare
Kickoff 2026-04-06 gives a development end around mid-July, leaving 6 weeks of buffer before the 2026-09-01 deadline.
